name: emailmd

hlido_opinion.headline: A neat, genuinely agent-native way to write responsive emails as Markdown — an MCP server lets any AI assistant draft, lint and render them, which is the clever part.
hlido_opinion.body: emailmd attacks a famously miserable problem — writing responsive HTML email that survives Outlook and every other client — with a pleasant premise: write Markdown (with a light directive syntax for headers, callouts, footers and front-matter), ship emails, 'no HTMHELL.' The captured surface is clean and developer-honest: templates, a builder, docs, an npm install path, and a live example showing a confirm-email template rendering from Markdown. The part that earns it a place in Hlido's corpus is the MCP server: any AI assistant (Claude Code, Claude.ai/Desktop, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code) can be given the tools to write, lint and render emails with a live preview link for every draft, one click to connect, or npx emailmd mcp locally. That's a real agent-to-agent surface, not a checkbox — it turns 'ask an AI to write a marketing email' into a linted, rendered, previewable artifact. The honest caveats are ordinary for a young dev tool: rendering fidelity across the messy world of email clients is the whole ballgame and can't be certified from the homepage, and the project's maturity/adoption and long-term maintenance aren't evidenced on the surface. For developers and AI-assisted teams who send transactional or marketing email, it's a genuinely useful, well-conceived tool.

tier_rationale: STEADY (72) for a clean, well-conceived tool that solves a real pain (responsive email without hand-written HTML) and ships a genuine agent surface (an MCP server that writes/lints/renders with live previews). Not higher because cross-client rendering fidelity — the core promise — can't be verified from the public surface, and maturity/adoption are unproven. Not FADING because the docs, builder and MCP integration show active, thoughtful development.
what_it_does_well: Write responsive emails in Markdown with a light directive syntax (headers, callouts, footers, front-matter) instead of hand-written HTML
MCP server lets AI assistants write, lint and render emails with a live preview link per draft — a real agent workflow
One-click connect for Claude Code / Claude.ai / ChatGPT / Cursor / VS Code, or npx emailmd mcp locally
Developer-honest surface: templates, a builder, docs, npm install, and a source-available GitHub repo
Live example (a confirm-email template) shows the Markdown-to-email rendering concretely
what_it_fails_at: Cross-client rendering fidelity (Outlook et al.) is the entire value and can't be verified from the homepage
Maturity/adoption and maintenance cadence aren't evidenced on the public surface
The directive syntax is a small new thing to learn versus a WYSIWYG builder for non-technical users
Deliverability, tracking and sending are out of scope — it renders, it doesn't send
best_for: Developers who want transactional/marketing email as version-controllable Markdown, not brittle HTML
AI-assisted teams who want an assistant to draft, lint and preview emails via MCP
Anyone who has fought Outlook rendering and wants a saner authoring layer
Teams standardising email templates in a repo with a builder and live previews
not_recommended_for: Non-technical marketers wanting a pure drag-and-drop builder with no syntax to learn
Teams needing an all-in-one ESP (sending, deliverability, analytics) — emailmd is the authoring/render layer only
Use cases that require certified cross-client rendering guarantees before adoption (test first)
red_flags: The core promise is cross-client responsive rendering, which is notoriously hard and is not demonstrated across clients on the public surface — validate against your real target clients before standardising on it.

compared_to.verdict_diff: MJML is the established markup framework for responsive email with wide adoption and tooling; emailmd trades MJML's XML-ish components for plainer Markdown plus, crucially, an MCP server so an AI assistant can author and render. Choose MJML for a proven ecosystem, emailmd for Markdown authoring + native agent integration.
